hero.headline: Tuition-free tech charter school opening in Fort Pierce in August
hero.body:
A new tuition-free career and technical charter school is preparing to open in Fort Pierce in August, bringing a hands-on approach to education to the Treasure Coast. SouthTech Treasure Coast will give middle and high school students the opportunity to earn industry certifications while completing their traditional coursework, helping them build real-world skills and prepare for high-demand careers before they graduate.

The St. Lucie County School Board approved the charter application for the Fort Pierce campus in April. School leaders say they selected the Treasure Coast because of the area's growing demand for skilled workers. The school will target high paying careers that are growing and expanding in the Fort Pierce area, said Nicole Handy, Director of Expansion of SouthTech Schools. The approach mirrors that of SouthTech Academy in Boynton Beach, which has spent years combining traditional academics with hands-on career training.

The Fort Pierce campus will serve students in grades 6 through 12, with plans to enroll about 460 students in its first year. Students will have the opportunity to choose from career academies including medical science, culinary arts, cosmetology, agriculture technology, and more. All students will work on their academics while enrolled in one of the career academies where they have the opportunity to earn adult level industry certifications while they are still in high school, said Carla Lovett, Executive Director of SouthTech Schools. The goal is to give students a head start on their careers by helping them graduate with valuable skills and certifications before entering the workforce or continuing their education. "It's better to learn something for free when you're a kid than to pay for it in college and learn, right?" said Meghan Hess Shamdasani, Career and Technical Education Program Coordinator.

SouthTech Treasure Coast will host a grand opening celebration on Saturday, July 25, from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m., giving families and community members a chance to tour the new campus and learn more about the programs being offered. SouthTech Treasure Coast in Fort Pierce is located at 2810 S. US Highway 1 Fort Pierce, FL 34982.

cards.headline: Child killed, another injured in bicycle collision with FedEx truck in Fort Pierce
cards.body:
A child died and another was hospitalized Monday afternoon after a bicycle collided with a FedEx truck in Fort Pierce, according to the Florida Highway Patrol.

The crash happened around 3:07 p.m. in the 600 block of East Midway Road. Two juveniles riding a bicycle collided with a FedEx truck. One child was pronounced dead at the scene. The second child was taken to a hospital in stable condition. Officials have not released the identities or ages of the children.

Neighbors who live near the scene said the area is commonly used by people riding bikes. Megan Sharma said she frequently sees children using the sidewalks on both sides of the road. "It's tragic, it's horrible. We see kids going up and down the sidewalk all the time. Both sides, our side and the opposite side. It's unfortunate that it happened," Sharma said. "It's really tragic that a child died." She also noted that tragedy has struck along East Midway Road before, recalling that several years ago in 2020, a young adult on a motorcycle was hit by a car. Sharma described the road as dangerous and urged caution. "Look both ways before you cross the street. Be weary of other vehicles, it's a dangerous, very dangerous highway," she said.

No additional details about what led up to the collision have been released. The Florida Highway Patrol continues to investigate the crash. This is a developing story and will be updated as more information becomes available.

cards.headline: Two men killed in Port St. Lucie shooting stemmed from jealousy over woman, police say
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie police said jealousy over a woman prompted an exchange of gunfire that claimed two lives early Sunday in the 1300 block of Southeast Rivergreen Circle.
cards.body:
Carl Loubeau, 24, and Juliun Stokes, 22, both from Fort Pierce, were found with multiple gunshot wounds in the driveways of a residence around 3:30 a.m. Sunday in the 1300 block of Southeast Rivergreen Circle. Both men were taken to separate local hospitals, where they later died from their injuries. Police said a verbal altercation occurred outside the residence over a key to a home and escalated into an exchange of gunfire between two of the individuals involved.

Chief Leo Niemczyk said a woman contacted Loubeau, whom she was dating, for a key because she was locked out of her home. When Loubeau arrived, he found her present with other people, including two males. Niemczyk said the motive behind the initial attack was jealousy over the female, with Loubeau as the primary aggressor in the dispute. Loubeau approached Stokes and opened fire on him, apparently mistaking Stokes for Dwayne Walker, 20. Walker was in close proximity and withdrew his firearm, which is lawfully carried, and started firing on Loubeau in self-defense. The current investigation shows Loubeau fired eight rounds from a 9 mm pistol and one round from a .380 pistol, while Walker fired eight rounds from his .40 caliber pistol. Walker was not injured in the incident. No arrests have been made in the case.

cards.headline: Stuart woman arrested after deputies rescue 80 cats from hoarding home in worst case sheriff has seen
cards.body:
Martin County deputies rescued dozens of cats Monday from a Stuart home that Sheriff John Budensiek described as the worst animal hoarding case he has seen in the county. The Martin County Sheriff's Office, Animal Control and Martin County Fire Rescue responded to a home in the 11500 block of Southwest Meadowlark Circle after an investigation into reports that a U.S. Postal Service employee had been collecting feral cats along her mail route.

Budensiek identified the homeowner as 77-year-old Gail Giustino. Investigators believe she was not stealing pets but was gathering feral cats and bringing them home. Authorities obtained a search warrant after Giustino allegedly refused to allow Animal Control officers inside the home during multiple attempts over the past week. When deputies entered the house Monday, they found what the sheriff described as horrific living conditions. The home had no working air conditioning, little to no ventilation and, in some areas, up to a foot of animal feces covering the floor. Budensiek said the odor was overwhelming, and Martin County Fire Rescue's Hazardous Materials Team had to ventilate the home before rescuers could safely enter.

Giustino told deputies she believed there were at least 70 cats inside the home, all kept in cages. Authorities believe there could ultimately be 70 to 80 animals or more, including several dogs, though an exact count had not been completed Monday evening. The rescued animals are being taken to the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast, which is expected to rely on foster families and volunteers to help care for them. Authorities said they are still evaluating the animals' medical conditions.

Budensiek said Giustino was arrested on two misdemeanor animal cruelty-related charges, though investigators said they could have pursued significantly more charges. The sheriff said the criminal charges were filed primarily to obtain the search warrant, remove the animals from the home and prevent Giustino from acquiring additional animals while she seeks help through the mental health court system. Budensiek said investigators believe Giustino had good intentions despite the terrible conditions. Officials said Animal Control had previously cited Giustino dozens of times for animal-related violations about 10 years ago, but they believe she gradually returned to hoarding animals after complying with earlier code enforcement requirements.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County firefighter firings questioned as police report contradicts hazing investigation
cards.teaser: Three St. Lucie County firefighters were terminated following an outside investigation into an alleged hazing incident, but a Fort Pierce Police report appears to reach a very different conclusion.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Fire Chief Jeff Lee issued a press release announcing the termination of three senior St. Lucie County firefighters following an investigation into an alleged hazing incident reported to the department in March 2026. An investigative summary prepared by an outside law firm hired by the St. Lucie County Fire District concluded that senior personnel had modified a bug zapper to shock three apprentice firefighters while on duty in 2024. The investigation was launched after six videos surfaced that the report says appeared to show hazing, workplace violence or other misconduct. Three supervisors were fired while two other firefighters were suspended.

A Fort Pierce Police report obtained by WPTV appears to reach a very different conclusion. A Fort Pierce police officer wrote that after interviewing the three firefighters who were shocked, there was no criminal matter behind the alleged hazing and that the videos showed coworkers entertaining each other. The report states the acts were done by their own will and that every person originally listed as a victim said they are not victims and did not want to continue the investigation. Retired Fire Captain Mike Jenkins, who served more than 30 years with the department, watched the videos and said he does not believe they show hazing. The St. Lucie County Chapter of the Professional Fire Fighters & Paramedics Union disputes the investigation, calling it biased and saying it reached a predetermined conclusion. Union President Ryan Sapp said the investigation was not conducted in an impartial or unbiased manner. The union is now demanding arbitration on behalf of the three firefighters who were terminated and the two others suspended.

cards.headline: Family files wrongful death lawsuit after 6-year-old killed in go-kart crash at Port St. Lucie Urban Air Adventure Park
cards.teaser: A wrongful death lawsuit was filed Monday against Urban Air Trampoline and Adventure Park in Port St. Lucie after 6-year-old Emma Riddle died in a go-kart crash at the facility in December 2025.
cards.body:
Emma Riddle, 6, was fatally injured at Urban Air Trampoline and Adventure Park in Port St. Lucie in December 2025. A wrongful death lawsuit was filed Monday against the business by the child's parents, who allege that Urban Air created dangerous conditions that contributed to Emma's death. Emma visited the adventure park with her mother and sister, where they rode electric go-karts. The child was seated with her mom in a double-seat go-kart while her older sister was in a single-rider go-kart. According to the family's attorney, Morgan & Morgan injury law firm, there were multiple alleged safety protocols ignored that allegedly led Emma's go-kart to accelerate to a high speed and crash into the track wall. Emma suffered severe injuries and was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where she later died.

Earlier this year, the Florida Department of Agriculture reached a $300,000 settlement agreement with Urban Air Adventure Park following an investigation into the fatal incident. The child's family claims the adventure park ignored safety rules and manufacturer guidelines. At 50 inches, Emma was nearly a foot shorter and twelve years younger than the manufacturer's minimum stated recommendations for operating a double-seat go-kart, and yet, she was permitted to ride, the lawsuit alleges. Morgan & Morgan founder John Morgan said Urban Air has a duty to protect every child that walks through their doors.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County firefighters' union disputes hazing findings, calls terminations unjust
cards.teaser: The union representing St. Lucie County Fire District firefighters is pushing back against the termination of three firefighters and suspension of two others, calling the investigation biased.
cards.body:
Professional Firefighters and Paramedics of St. Lucie County, IAFF Local 1377, said the St. Lucie County Fire District wrongly terminated and suspended the five members for their involvement in incidents that occurred in March and September 2024. Local 1377 President Ryan Sapp stated in a letter obtained by WPTV that these incidents did not involve any hazing. Sapp pointed to the Fort Pierce Police Department's report, which he said described the situation, in part, as "found coworkers entertaining each other." The union's position is that all five were wrongly found to be in violation of fire district policies and disciplined without just cause.

The union raised concerns about the outside law firm the fire district hired to conduct its investigation, Allen, Norton & Blue. Local 1377 and its legal counsel said the investigation was not conducted in an impartial or unbiased manner. Sapp stated in the letter that the nature of the questions asked, as well as the way in which they were asked or not asked, reflects a predetermined conclusion rather than an objective fact-finding process. Sapp noted that the same firm that conducted the investigation has since been hired by the fire district to represent it at arbitration. Local 1377 has demanded arbitration for all five members and said it remains willing to negotiate a reasonable resolution that would avoid the significant costs of arbitration and save both the taxpayers and the union a substantial amount of money.

cards.headline: Murray Middle School demolition begins after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
cards.teaser: Murray Middle School demolition is underway in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton.
cards.body:
Murray Middle School demolition is underway in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The project includes reconstruction of buildings destroyed in the tornadoes, along with a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a full overhaul of the parking lot. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not been finalized.

 The project is being funded by local capital improvement, sales tax and Public Education Capital Outlay. Students who were displaced from the affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete.

 Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, said Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab. With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine, the district was able to add these on.

 The school district said parents can be assured their students will be safe during construction. Barriers have already been placed around the work zone to keep students out. The district hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County residents adjust diets as E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks spread
cards.teaser: Health officials confirmed five local cases of cyclospora since May, including two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County, prompting residents to change what they eat and avoid.
cards.body:
Concerns over contaminated produce linked to E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks are prompting South Florida residents to reconsider their food choices, with some avoiding leafy greens entirely. The outbreaks have affected thousands nationwide and include lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. Health officials have confirmed local cases stretching from the Palm Beaches to the Treasure Coast, including two cases in St. Lucie County.

 The Florida Department of Health reported five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May. Two cases were reported in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County, and one in Martin County. The contamination concerns have led families across the region to change their eating habits at restaurants, grocery stores, and fast-food chains.

 Dakota and Brynlee Rhodes, who were visiting Delray Beach with their mother Jenny, said they are trying to stay away from lettuce and stuff like that. Other families are similarly steering clear of leafy greens altogether as reports of contaminated produce continue to spread across the country. The widespread nature of the outbreaks has left many consumers uncertain about which products are safe to purchase and consume.

 Samantha Barone, a dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, offered guidance for consumers looking to maintain healthy diets while avoiding potentially contaminated produce. Barone recommends sticking to melon and things that have a harder skin that you can peel. She advises consumers to focus on produce with protective outer layers and to wash all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them.

 For those seeking alternatives to leafy greens, Barone suggests that beans and nuts are safe options that still provide fiber and protein. She specifically recommends cleaning produce using a mixture of one part distilled white vinegar to three parts water. The outbreaks have highlighted the importance of proper food handling and preparation practices for consumers across South Florida.

cards.headline: Boynton Beach firefighters rescue dog from raw sewage lift station
cards.teaser: A dog fell roughly 10 to 12 feet into a lift station holding about 2 feet of raw sewage Thursday, prompting a specialized confined space rescue.
cards.body:
A dog fell roughly 10 to 12 feet into a lift station holding about 2 feet of raw sewage Thursday, prompting a specialized confined space rescue by Boynton Beach Fire Rescue Department. Squad 6 crews arrived and assessed the scene before upgrading the incident to a Special Operations confined space rescue, the department said. Firefighters developed a rescue plan and had Firefighter Ramirez properly rigged and ready to enter the lift station.

 From the time he went on air, Firefighter Ramirez rescued the dog and safely exited the lift station in just 4 minutes, the department said. Once above ground, crews decontaminated the dog and gave it oxygen before turning it over to Animal Control. Animal Control successfully reunited the dog with its owner, according to a Facebook post from the department.

cards.headline: Wellington teen injured after electric bike rider strikes him during stunt near Lion Country Safari
cards.teaser: A Wellington teenager suffered multiple injuries, including broken bones, after being struck by an electric bike rider performing a wheelie on Tuesday night.
cards.body:
Seventeen-year-old Chad Filer said he was riding his scooter along a relatively isolated stretch of road between the Deer Run community and Lion Country Safari on Tuesday night when three teenage boys on dirt and electric bikes approached him. According to Chad, one rider began performing a wheelie and intentionally swerved toward him in what he described as a common "bike life" stunt meant to intimidate people before pulling away at the last second, but instead the bike struck the right side of his body.

 Chad estimates the rider was traveling around 40 mph when the impact sent him to the ground. A driver stopped to help, and Chad said the riders initially stayed nearby and told him he was "fine," but once witnesses called 911, the group fled.

 Doctors found Chad suffered broken metatarsal bones, three broken toes, significant bruising and multiple road rash injuries across his chest, knee, elbow and side. His mother, Cortez Hornsby, said part of one nipple was partially detached in the crash. The family faces mounting medical expenses because Chad's health insurance through work was not scheduled to begin until next month.

 Hornsby says she called the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office and was told this is a county-wide problem. She also says deputies told her that based on how isolated the crash site is and the lack of cameras, it may be difficult to find the teens. Chad cannot work while he heals, and the scooter he relied on for transportation was heavily damaged.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District releases hazing investigation reports, 3 firefighters terminated
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Fire District released investigative reports Saturday detailing allegations of hazing and workplace misconduct that led to the termination of 3 firefighters and the suspension of 2 others.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District on Saturday released investigative reports detailing allegations of hazing and workplace misconduct. Administrators first received videos in March 2026 showing what they described as senior firefighters using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to probationary and apprentice firefighters while on duty. The district said the incidents occurred during shifts in March and September 2024. The videos prompted Fire Chief Jeff Lee to hire an outside attorney to conduct an independent investigation rather than handle the matter internally.

Attorney J.K. Keller, of Allen, Norton & Blue, concluded that a preponderance of the evidence showed probationary employees had been subjected to hazing by senior firefighters and supervisors. Keller also determined the conduct violated multiple district policies, including workplace violence and employee conduct rules. The investigative report describes videos showing probationary firefighters being questioned while connected to the modified device and receiving electrical shocks when they answered incorrectly. Other videos allegedly show probationary firefighters voluntarily allowing themselves to be shocked while coworkers looked on. Investigators concluded that any claimed consent was undermined by the power imbalance between senior firefighters and probationary employees. The district followed Keller's recommendations by terminating 3 employees and issuing 48-hour unpaid suspensions to 2 others. The disciplined employees have exercised their contractual rights to challenge the actions through the grievance and arbitration process.

cards.headline: Waterspouts, lightning strikes and fires batter Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County
cards.teaser: Friday's severe weather left a trail of impacts across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County, including waterspouts in Sebastian, lightning strikes and brush fires in Port St. Lucie.
cards.body:
Friday's severe weather left a trail of impacts across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. Video sent to the WPTV newsroom from Sebastian showed a large waterspout passing over the Indian River Lagoon Friday afternoon. In Port St. Lucie, WPTV weather spotters captured video of heavy rain moving through the area. Merry Moore O'Rourke said her rain gauge caught over 3 inches. Moore O'Rourke described the sudden change in conditions, saying it got black, the wind started raging and the sky lit up like she had not seen.

Severe weather stretched to Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning. Port St. Lucie also saw significant lightning activity. Lucie County Fire District said crews contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after reports that a lightning strike ignited vegetation in a nearby lot. At the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue, fire crews responded to an evening house fire. Lucie County Fire District said it cannot confirm the cause, as the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate. Moore O'Rourke said the storms were radical and a little scary.

The report also states the acts were done by their own will, and that every person originally listed as a victim said they are not victims and did not want to continue the investigation. Retired Fire Captain Mike Jenkins, who served more than 30 years with the department, watched the videos and said he does not believe they show hazing. Jenkins was one of several people who spoke at last week's fire board meeting, calling the incident a harmless, consensual prank. The St. Lucie County Chapter of the Professional Fire Fighters & Paramedics Union disputes the investigation, calling it biased and saying it reached a predetermined conclusion.

hero.headline: JetBlue ending Vero Beach to JFK route in September due to low demand
hero.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates and that JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He praised the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach, saying "It's easy. It's close." Meanwhile, Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time, and Dambeck said that route is performing well with great demand.

Dambeck said the door is not closed for the JFK route to return in the future. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said. He noted that air carriers will fluctuate based on demand, explaining that this is simply how the market works. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service.

All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information. The airline will continue serving Vero Beach through its Boston route, which is seeing strong performance compared to the canceled JFK service.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie couple fights rezoning of lot behind their home, says voices went unheard
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie couple is searching for answers after the city council voted to rezone the lot behind their home from residential to commercial, despite their months-long opposition.
cards.body:
The Mucciolos have called Port St. Lucie home for years, drawn to the property by its beautiful setting and backyard views of nature. In a unanimous vote, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved changing the lot behind their yard, where trees currently stand, to be rezoned from residential to commercial. The council says the change is necessary to reduce traffic in the neighborhood.

 One council member said adding commercial closer to neighborhoods reduces the length of trips, which reduces overall traffic because shorter trips reduce the burden on the overall network. Joseph Mucciolo said the trees will be gone in six months or a year.

 The two spoke at Monday's meeting, voicing their concerns, but they feel the council left them unheard. The council held its second reading Monday. While there was public comment, it was what's called a quasi-judicial hearing, meaning council members act as a panel of judges, applying existing zoning rules to a specific property and making decisions based strictly on sworn testimony and factual evidence, not public opinion.

 Joseph Mucciolo said the couple fought for months and feels their voices have gone unheard except for the news media. The Mucciolos say they will be exploring any kind of appeal process to change this outcome or to change the next one. Margaret Mucciolo said the process needs to change until it's logical, transparent, caring, and provides hope for people.
